title: Hand & Power Tool Safety
blurb: Using hand and power tools safely: competence, inspection, guards, PPE and safe use.
siteNotes: Who confirms you are trained and competent on each tool.
How faulty tools are tagged and reported, and where tools are stored.
Which PPE is issued, and where to get it.
legalNotes: The trainer rests on general good practice for work equipment (Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998); no regulation is quoted on the slides and no figures are stated.

cards.title: Hand & Power Tool Safety
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- use only the right tool, and only if competent
- inspect tools and report faults
- use PPE and power tools safely

cards.title: Right tool, right person
cards.body:
Hand and power tools make maintenance work quick and effective, but they cause serious injuries when misused or poorly maintained.

Only use tools you have been trained and are competent to use, and always use the right tool for the job. Improvising with the wrong tool is a common cause of accidents.

items.title: Trained
items.text: Only tools you are competent to use

cards.title: Inspect every tool
cards.body:
Inspect tools before you use them. Look for damage: cracked casings, frayed cables, blunt or chipped blades, loose heads.

Take anything faulty out of use and report it. Make sure guards are fitted and working, and never remove or defeat a guard to work faster.

items.title: Check
items.text: Blades and heads, blunt or loose

items.title: Faulty?
items.text: Take out of use and report

cards.title: Protect yourself
cards.body: Wear the right PPE for the task. Eye protection is a must for anything that cuts, grinds or drills, plus gloves, ear defenders and dust protection where needed.

cards.title: Clamp it, keep clear
cards.body: Secure the workpiece, for example in a clamp, rather than holding it by hand. Keep your hands and body clear of the cutting line.

left.title: Do
items: Keep hands clear of the cutting line
Keep your body clear of the cutting line

cards.title: Power, cables and stopping
cards.body:
Disconnect from the power before changing blades, bits or discs. Keep cables clear of the work and walkways, and never carry a tool by its cable.

Let cutting tools stop completely before putting them down. Store tools safely and keep them clean and sharp.

items.title: Disconnect
items.text: Before changing blades, bits or discs

items.title: Cables
items.text: Clear of the work and walkways

items.title: Carry
items.text: By the body, never the cable

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Only use tools you are trained and competent to use, and use the right tool for the job.
- Inspect before use; take faulty tools out of use and report them.
- Never remove or defeat a guard.
- Wear the right PPE, and secure the workpiece.
- Disconnect power before changing blades, bits or discs; never carry a tool by its cable.

cards.q: You should only use tools you have been trained and are competent to use.
cards.why: The foundation is simple: only use tools you have been trained and are competent to use.

cards.q: What should you do with a faulty or damaged tool?
options: Use it carefully for the last job
Tape it up and carry on
Take it out of use and report it
Put it back for someone else to find
cards.why: Take anything faulty out of use and report it.

cards.q: Before changing a blade or bit on a power tool you should…
options: Disconnect it from the power
Keep it running at low speed
Hold the trigger half down
Wait for the blade to cool and carry on
cards.why: Disconnect from the power before changing blades, bits or discs.

cards.q: It is acceptable to remove a guard to work faster.
cards.why: Make sure guards are fitted and working, and never remove or defeat a guard to work faster.

cards.q: Which of these is PPE for using cutting or grinding tools?
options: A hi-vis vest
A hard hat on its own
A baseball cap
Eye protection
cards.why: Eye protection is a must for anything that cuts, grinds or drills.

cards.q: You should secure the workpiece, for example in a clamp, rather than holding it by hand.
cards.why: Secure the workpiece rather than holding it by hand, and keep your hands clear of the cutting line.

cards.q: You should carry a power tool by…
options: Its cable, to keep hands free
Its handle or body, not the cable
Its blade or bit, near the guard
Whichever part is nearest to hand
cards.why: Never carry a tool by its cable.

cards.q: Using the wrong tool for the job is a common cause of accidents.
cards.why: Improvising with the wrong tool is a common cause of accidents.

cards.q: What should you look for when inspecting a tool before use?
options: Whether it is the newest model on site
Whether it matches the other tools
Damage such as a frayed cable or cracked casing
Whether it looks clean and shiny
cards.why: Look for damage: cracked casings, frayed cables, blunt or chipped blades, loose heads.

cards.q: Let a cutting tool stop completely before you put it down.
cards.why: Let cutting tools stop completely before putting them down.
